title: Wargame Orchestrator for VPC Recovery Scenarios
creator: Ava Morgan
description:
Goal: Build an automated 'wargame' orchestrator that runs repeatable recovery scenarios against Private (VPC) deployments. The orchestrator will compose Terraform IaC changes, runtime upgrade exercises, and end-to-end health checks to validate cross-region continuity and failover behavior.

Why: Current DR validation for Private customers is manual, brittle, and expensive to run. This work reduces human toil, provides reproducible evidence for customers and SRE, and closes the gap between our documented runbooks and what actually happens during a regional outage.

Scope: - Scenario templating (region isolation, control-plane switch, instance drain, data-plane rehoming)
- Terraform automation hooks (safe plan/apply with tear-down or rollback)
- Synthetic traffic generator and KV/cache warmers to validate correctness under load
- Health and reconciliation checks (DNS, network routes, KMS access, model artifacts availability)
- Observability dashboards and post-run artifacts (timings, token cost delta, error rates)
- Safety guardrails (staging-only by default, approval gate for prod, post-mortem checklist)

Out-of-scope: Full productized UI for customers; this is an internal orchestration runner and job set that can be exposed later through the Console.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A runnable 'wargame' job can be triggered from CI or CLI that performs a predefined scenario against a Private VPC deployment in staging.
2. The job composes Terraform modules to enact the scenario (e.g., simulate region unavailability by adjusting routing/peering or draining instances) and can cleanly revert changes.
3. During the run, synthetic traffic validates latency and correctness and collects metrics; a pass/fail evaluation is produced based on preconfigured SLO thresholds.
4. Post-run artifacts (terraform plan/apply logs, perf traces, error samples, dashboard links) are uploaded to a run artifact bucket and linked in the job summary.
5. Safety: prod gating requires manual approval and an abort path; accidental prod runs must be detectable and rollbackable.
6. Run completes within bounded time for each scenario type (target < 90m for basic failover; < 6h for complex upgrade+failover scenarios).
7. Documentation: runbook added to Confluence with step-by-step guidance and a checklist for on-call handoff.
8. Observability: Dashboard with run timeline, KV-cache hit rates, model artifact availability, and request error breakdown is provisioned and linked.
implementation_plan: Design scenario templates (regional isolation, control-plane switchover, rolling upgrade + eviction) and canonical preconditions.
Extend existing Terraform IaC modules with 'orchestration hooks' (variables to simulate network partition, instance drain tags, peering toggles) and safe revert plans.
Build a small orchestration binary (Go) that executes scenario steps: dry-run terraform plan -> apply (with approvals) -> traffic generator -> health checks -> revert or escalate.
Integrate job runner with CI (GitHub Actions workflow) and internal Runner queue for scheduling repeatable drills.
Implement synthetic traffic generator (python/locust prototype) with workload profiles matching common customer patterns and KV-cache/embedding warmers.
Create health-check suite: DNS resolve checks, route table verification, KMS envelope sign/verify test, model artifact fetch test, token-level request smoke tests.
Wire observability: run-specific tags in tracing, pull aggregate metrics and generate run artifacts; post results to a Slack channel and Confluence page.
Add approval gate: require an explicit PR + GitHub approval for prod-targeted runs; add safety toggles in orchestration config to disable destructive steps unless explicitly enabled.
Run initial wargame against staging, capture learnings, iterate on failure modes and revert logic.
Promote the runner into a restricted prod-on-call workflow after a security review and runbook sign-off.
Postmortem and checklist creation after every run; maintain a repository of scenario outcomes for regression detection.
Deliverables: orchestration binary, Terraform module patches, traffic generator, dashboards, runbook, and CI workflows.
Owner: Diego Patel; SRE reviewer: Samir Banerjee; Security reviewer: Riley Chen; PM: Nora Alvarez.
terraform_changes: Add 'orchestrator_mode' variable to private/vpc modules to simulate graceful instance draining and route blackholing (safe default: false).
Create 'wargame' submodule that exposes hooks for toggling peering, BGP advertisements, and load-balancer weights via terraform apply.
Implement idempotent revert plans using remote-state snapshots and a 'replay' helper to rebuild previous routing state if revert fails.
Add fine-grained IAM roles for the orchestration CI service principal with least privilege (plan/apply, read-state, tagging) and separate prod/staging service principals.
Add integration tests to terratest suite that run the minimal plan in a sandbox namespace to validate non-destructive changes.
Document Terraform provider version constraints and add a provider upgrade check to CI to avoid drift during orchestration runs.
test_plan: Unit tests for orchestration step sequencing and failure recovery paths.
Integration tests: run a dry-run scenario against a disposable staging VPC using GitHub Actions; validate revert path works on simulated failure.
E2E validation: run full wargame in staging with synthetic traffic and assert SLO targets; record token/cost delta for billing analysis.
Chaos tests: in a dedicated sandbox, randomly inject partial failures (DNS latency, simulated KMS error) to ensure orchestrator can detect and escalate.
Acceptance: SRE and PM sign-off on at least 2 successful staging runs before we consider ad-hoc prod gating.
observability: Dashboard (grafana) tile: wargame-run timeline with step boundaries and durations.
Traces: tag all orchestration API calls with run-id; collect open-telemetry spans for terraform apply/plan calls.
Metrics: KV cache hit rate, model artifact fetch latency, request error rate during synthetic traffic, route reconciliation time.
Artifacts: link to artifacts bucket (s3://redwood-wargame-archives/{run-id}) that contains terraform logs, runner stdout, perf profiles, and test reports.
Alerts: failed health-check post-run produces PagerDuty incident only if run targeted prod; staging failures post to #infra-wargame without PD.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Terraform apply could make destructive changes in prod. Mitigation: require manual approval, use service principals with scoped perms, and run apply in a sandbox first.

Risk: Synthetic traffic could spike costs or impact real customers. Mitigation: run traffic from dedicated sandbox subnets isolated by routing and throttles; default to replay cached payloads rather than generate cold requests.
Risk: KMS or external dependencies fail during run and mask true behavior. Mitigation: include short-circuit checks and an escalation policy; snapshot run-state before destructive steps.
Risk: Drift between IaC and prod state. Mitigation: run a pre-check that compares live state to remote-state and pauses run on >X% drift.
